doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cal Massey, Coltrane and the Jazztet
title: The turnpike breakdown story and Miles raising Coltrane's pay
summary: Brown relays Golson's story of Coltrane picking up Tyner after a car breakdown; Tyner says Miles kept raising Coltrane's salary to keep him.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: There was a story--and I’m going to ask Ken to fill in the details--but when we interviewed Benny, he said that you were driving on the turnpike and your car broke down and I think you called Benny and Benny couldn’t come get you and I guess he arranged for John to come pick you up.

Yeah, that’s right, they knew each other because they were from the same part of town, North Philly. So they knew each other and for some reason he called John. I guess John knew that we had a musical relationship even though I hadn’t joined his band yet, I was still with the Jazztet. But they knew each other, they weren’t hostile toward each other.
Did Benny stay on the turnpike leaving from Philly to go to New York?
So who’s that guy walking around the turnpike with all those bags!?
The way Benny tells it is, that’s the way you hooked up with John because he came to get you, but I don’t know.

Every time John wanted to leave and form his own band, Miles would up his salary, I don’t think Miles wanted him to leave. He wanted to form his own band you know, “Hold up buddy” (laughs) . . . I couldn’t blame Miles for that, but John wanted to leave and start his own band because he had his own ideas.
Oh yeah, Benny can tell some stories.
If you want an elaboration, he can do it, yeah he’s like that.
